claims.claim: The 1996 Publishers Weekly review calls A Game of Thrones conventional in form.
claims.source: Publishers Weekly (unsigned starred review), A Game of Thrones, 29 July 1996

claims.claim: Paul Levinson's 1996 Tangent review praises Martin for writing convincingly of tart juices oozing from an apple and of sleet on a mountainside.
claims.source: Paul Levinson, review of A Game of Thrones, Tangent #16, Fall 1996 (reposted by the author)
claims.quote: tart juices oozing from an apple as of sleet

claims.claim: Levinson's 1996 review says A Game of Thrones is as much an adventure of the senses as of the mind.
claims.source: Paul Levinson, review of A Game of Thrones, Tangent #16, Fall 1996 (reposted by the author)
claims.quote: as much an adventure of the senses as it is

claims.claim: Levinson's 1996 review calls the settings of A Game of Thrones equally diverse and evocative.
claims.source: Paul Levinson, review of A Game of Thrones, Tangent #16, Fall 1996 (reposted by the author)
claims.quote: The settings are equally diverse and evocative.

claims.claim: Levinson's 1996 review says the descriptive passages of the Daenerys thread let the reader smell and taste the spice in the wine.
claims.source: Paul Levinson, review of A Game of Thrones, Tangent #16, Fall 1996 (reposted by the author)
claims.quote: you can smell the spice, and taste it in every

claims.claim: Levinson's 1996 review argues that the on-page appearance of Martin's cold creatures has far less impact than their suggestion.
claims.source: Paul Levinson, review of A Game of Thrones, Tangent #16, Fall 1996 (reposted by the author)
claims.quote: has far less impact than their suggestion

claims.claim: Levinson's 1996 review says Martin's dragons work better as natural history, their skeletons admired, feared and lamented by characters, than as living hatchlings.
claims.source: Paul Levinson, review of A Game of Thrones, Tangent #16, Fall 1996 (reposted by the author)
claims.quote: their skeletons are admired, feared, and lamented by various characters

claims.claim: Steve Jeffery's 1997 Vector review attributes the episodic feel of A Game of Thrones's later stretches to Martin's alternation of chapters between major viewpoint characters.
claims.source: Steve Jeffery, review of A Game of Thrones, Vector 192 (BSFA), March/April 1997, p.19
claims.quote: Martin's technique of alternating chapters between a number of major viewpoint characters

claims.claim: Jeffery's 1997 Vector review lists an appendix cast list among the distinguishing features of A Game of Thrones as a fantasy blockbuster.
claims.source: Steve Jeffery, review of A Game of Thrones, Vector 192 (BSFA), March/April 1997, p.19
claims.quote: an Appendix listing a cast of Cecil B. DeMille

claims.feature: other: marketing hype versus the book
claims.claim: Jeffery's 1997 Vector review rejects the jacket blurb's 'true heir to Tolkien' framing as gushing hype that does the book no favours.
claims.source: Steve Jeffery, review of A Game of Thrones, Vector 192 (BSFA), March/April 1997, p.19
claims.quote: This sort of gushing hype does no favours to anybody,

claims.claim: The 2011 Publishers Weekly review of A Dance with Dragons identifies a few recurring images — the game cyvasse, small rivers flowing into larger ones, and storm-battered ships and armies — running through the book.
claims.source: Publishers Weekly (unsigned), A Dance with Dragons, 30 May 2011
claims.quote: A few images recur in the enormously complex fifth installment

claims.claim: Kirkus's 2011 review calls the dialogue of A Dance with Dragons the usual swords-and-sorcery dialogue and quotes three lines as its evidence.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews (unsigned), A Dance with Dragons, posted online 26 September 2011

claims.claim: Kirkus's 2011 review describes the exposition in A Dance with Dragons as sometimes seemingly endless.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews (unsigned), A Dance with Dragons, posted online 26 September 2011
claims.quote: the usual blend of exposition, sometimes seemingly endless

claims.claim: Kirkus's 2011 review says Tolkien was never as ponderous as Martin.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews (unsigned), A Dance with Dragons, posted online 26 September 2011
claims.quote: Tolkien was never quite so ponderous

claims.claim: Kirkus's 2011 review charges Martin with being obsessed with bodily functions of various sorts, quoting two lines as evidence.
claims.source: Kirkus Reviews (unsigned), A Dance with Dragons, posted online 26 September 2011
claims.quote: so obsessed with bodily functions of various sorts
